how_to_read: One entry per question. 'covered' says whether the lease answers it. 'answer' is the right answer in plain words. 'points' are what a right answer must convey, judged by meaning: any wording counts. 'mistakes' are wrong answers a reader could fall into, each of which makes the answer wrong. 'passages' are the lease's own words that answer it, copied exactly; they are used to check quotations, which must be word for word. 'absent_words' must be nowhere in the lease, for a question it does not answer. 'note' says what makes the question hard.

questions.question: My rent will be paid on the 7th this month. Do I owe a late fee, and how much?
questions.answer: Yes. Rent not paid by the end of the 5th owes a $40.00 late fee.
points: A late fee is owed, because rent is late once the 5th has passed.
The late fee is $40.00.
mistakes: Says no late fee is owed.
Gives a late fee amount other than $40.00.
passages: If rent is not paid by the end of the 5th day of the month, the Tenant owes a late fee of $40.00.

questions.question: Can I keep a cat in my room?
questions.answer: No. No pets of any kind; the only exception is fish in one tank of 10 gallons or less.
points: No, a cat is not allowed, because the lease bans pets of any kind.
mistakes: Says a cat is allowed, or allowed with the landlord's permission.
passages: No pets of any kind may be kept in the house or yard, even for a short visit.

points: Deliver it by hand or send it by mail.
Send it to Patricia Nguyen at 2840 NW 16th Boulevard, Gainesville, Florida 32605.
mistakes: Says a text or email is enough for this notice.
passages: A formal written notice to the Landlord, such as a notice about the lease or about the deposit, must be delivered by hand or sent by mail to Patricia Nguyen, 2840 NW 16th Boulevard, Gainesville, Florida 32605.
questions.note: Near miss: the same clause allows text or email for day-to-day messages.

questions.note: Option 1 offers a $3,700.00 fee, but its initials line is blank.

questions.question: I plan to move out when the lease ends. Do I need to give notice?
questions.answer: Yes. Written notice at least 60 days before the Expiration Date, or owe one month's rent as liquidated damages.
points: Yes, written notice at least 60 days before the Expiration Date.
mistakes: Says no notice is needed.
Gives a notice period other than 60 days.
passages: Either Party wishing to terminate the tenancy at the Expiration Date shall give the other Party written notice at least sixty (60) days before the Expiration Date.

questions.question: Do I have to pay for small repairs myself?
questions.answer: The first $100.00 of any single repair not caused by the landlord's neglect, wear and tear, or a structural defect.
points: The tenant pays the first $100.00 of any single repair (not caused by the landlord's neglect, ordinary wear and tear, or a structural defect).
mistakes: Says the tenant pays nothing for repairs.
Says the tenant pays all small repairs in full.
passages: Tenant shall pay the first $100.00 of the cost of any single repair not caused by Landlord's neglect, ordinary wear and tear, or structural defect.

questions.question: My friend wants to stay with us for three weeks. Is that OK?
questions.answer: Not without the landlord's prior written consent: no one else may stay more than 14 days in a row or 30 days a year.
points: Not without the landlord's prior written consent, because no other person may stay more than 14 days in a row (or 30 days a year).
mistakes: Says a three-week stay is allowed without consent.
passages: No other person may reside at the Premises for more than fourteen (14) consecutive days, or more than thirty (30) days in any calendar year, without Landlord's prior written consent.

questions.question: Can I sublet the house while I travel this summer?
questions.answer: Only with the landlord's prior written consent, which the landlord may refuse for any reason.
points: Only with the landlord's prior written consent, which the landlord may withhold in its sole discretion.
mistakes: Says subletting is allowed without consent.
Says subletting is never allowed.
passages: Tenant shall not assign this Lease, sublet all or any part of the Premises, or license any person to occupy the Premises without Landlord's prior written consent, which Landlord may withhold in its sole discretion.

questions.question: Does the lease limit how much the landlord can raise the rent if I renew?
questions.answer: The lease does not say.
points: The lease does not address the rent for a renewal.
mistakes: Says the lease caps or sets the rent for a renewal.
questions.note: Near miss: Section 2.3 says the lease does not renew automatically, and Section 2.4 keeps the same terms in a month-to-month holdover. Mentioning them is fine.

questions.question: Does the lease say anything about package deliveries?
questions.answer: The lease does not say.
points: The lease does not address package deliveries.
mistakes: Describes package rules as if the lease had them.
